chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
‘The one who performs the ritual bath for major impurity but does not wash his head, then it occurs to him that he should wash his head, must not find an alternative but to repeat the ritual bath.’

key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: The ritual full-body bath required for purification
key_terms.جَنَابَةٍ: Major ritual impurity, typically from sexual intercourse or ejaculation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to wash their head during the ritual bath for major impurity?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudential view that the head is an integral part of the body for ghusl; thus, omitting it invalidates the entire ritual bath rather than constituting a mere deficiency. It highlights the principle that ghusl for janabah requires the washing of the entire body, including the head, as a unified act, distinguishing it from wudu where the head is washed separately. This ruling underscores the importance of completeness in purificatory acts within the Ja'fari school of thought.
